D12·kfkr — 2026-09-16
rule: Every launch writes a ledger row before it starts and one after it ends; an attempt with no reported cost is charged at the next-session estimate, never zero; no launch proceeds past a per-run or rolling cap without a recorded pause.
chose: 3.2 contract — the DURABLE SPEND LEDGER, settled before code. (1) ONE append-only JSONL across every run: ~/IO/bench-cells/evaluator/ledger.jsonl, written only by the evaluator process (inside the candidate's write-denied store). Kinds: pack, controls, score (time only, no model), launch_intent (BEFORE a launch), launch_outcome (after: ok, timed out, exit, ms, turns, tokens, reported cost), launch_lost (an intent the process never closed, written on resume or reconcile), refusal, stop. The run-local results/attempts.jsonl stays as a filtered copy. (2) EVERY ATTEMPT COSTS SOMETHING, never zero: a launch is REPORTED (claude -p's total_cost_usd), UNKNOWN (an outcome with no usage) or OPEN (an intent with no outcome — the evaluator died, the machine slept, the operator killed it). Unknown and open attempts are charged at the next-session estimate (`--next-session-usd`, default $8, the same headroom figure the round-1 runner uses) in every cap check and reported apart from reported spend, with their counts. Controls, packs and scoring count as attempts with time but no model cost — the whole improvement cost (self-improve D1 addition C) includes them. (3) CAPS, checked before EVERY launch and stated on the run's stream: per-run `--max-usd` (default $20) on the run's cumulative spend across restarts; the bench-refresh D17 rolling caps — 7-day $450 and 5-hour $150 — over Claude spend computed the runner's way (claude-code arms, reported cost, ended inside the window) over the round-1 ledgers PLUS this ledger, so the evaluator's spend counts against the operator's half-limit; `--max-launches` (default sessions × reps, lost attempts included) bounds no-progress retries. A cap hit is a PAUSE (exit 4, a `stop` row with the reason, resumable), a billing/limit signal is a STOP (exit 3, D14), and neither is ever silent. (4) RESTART-SAFE: `run --run <id> --resume` re-verifies pin, controls and the sandbox self-test, skips every (rep, session) that already has a result, closes open intents with launch_lost, resets the cell repo to its last bench commit (git reset --hard + clean, as the round-1 runner does) before relaunching, and charges the lost attempt. (5) LIMITS STATED: the round-1 runner does not read this ledger, so ITS caps exclude evaluator spend while the evaluator's include both; costs are what the agent reports on a subscription (API-equivalent, not billed); only claude-code is metered here.
over: Reusing the runner's per-round ledger.json (a mutable snapshot the runner owns; not append-only; not readable as a cross-run stream); a per-run ledger only (a restart or a second run loses the cross-run view D17 needs); counting an unattributed attempt as $0 (audit S6: include unattributed failures and unavailable-cost cases); a hard stop on a rolling cap (the runner pauses, and pacing is not a billing event — D17).
because: Audit S6 asks for a finite experiment budget across every launch, retry, resume and evaluator run, including unattributed failures and unavailable-cost cases, with enforceable bounds and stated limits; D1's addition C says improvement claims are net of the WHOLE cost, which is only computable from a ledger that saw every attempt. Charging unknown and open attempts at the estimate errs toward under-spending the operator's limit, the direction bench-refresh D17 chose. Aligning the rolling arithmetic with budget.ts means one number means the same thing in both tools.
